A 26-year-old male arrives at the emergency department following a low-speed motor vehicle collision
where his stationary vehicle was struck from behind by a car traveling at 11 miles per hour. He reports
intense back pain but denies other symptoms. His medical history reveals ongoing physical therapy for
back pain that is most severe in the mornings, improves with physical activity, and worsens during
periods of inactivity. He is a university student experiencing academic difficulties. His vital signs show:
temperature 99.4°F (36.9°C), blood pressure 107/68 mmHg, pulse 103/min, respirations 15/min, and
oxygen saturation 99% on room air. Physical examination reveals spinal tenderness and limited range
of motion, with the remainder of the examination limited by pain. The patient is seeking documentation
to be excused from his final examinations and work duties. What is the most probable diagnosis?
Answer Choices: (A) Herniated nucleus pulposus (B) Psychogenic pain disorder (C) Acute disc
herniation (D) Musculoskeletal strain (E) Spondylolisthesis (F) Factitious disorder (G) Conversion
disorder (H) Malingering (I) Spinal cord contusion (J) Vertebral fracture
 A. Conversion disorder
B. Psychogenic pain disorder
C. Malingering
D. Factitious disorder

E. Acute disc herniation
F. Spinal cord contusion
G. Spondylolisthesis
H. Musculoskeletal strain
I. Vertebral fracture
J. Herniated nucleus pulposus
